sections.normalized_html: The point [MATH: P] with coordinates [MATH: (2, -1)] lies on the curve [MATH: y=f(x)]. Which point must lie on the graph of [MATH: y= -f(x)?]
sections.readable_text: The point [MATH: P] with coordinates [MATH: (2, -1)] lies on the curve [MATH: y=f(x)]. Which point must lie on the graph of [MATH: y= -f(x)?]

sections.normalized_html:
The transformation [MATH: y=-f(x)] reflects the curve [MATH: y=f(x)] in the [MATH: x]-axis.

First, notice that the point [MATH: P(2, -1)] lies [MATH: 1] unit below the [MATH: x]-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected [MATH: 1] unit above the [MATH: x]-axis.

We conclude that the point [MATH: (2,1)] must lie on the graph of [MATH: y=-f(x).]

Item 5 — Example: Identifying a Point on a Vertically Reflected Function

Example Prompt:
The point [MATH: P] with coordinates [MATH: (2, -1)] lies on the curve [MATH: y=f(x)]. Which point must lie on the graph of [MATH: y= -f(x)?]

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The transformation [MATH: y=-f(x)] reflects the curve [MATH: y=f(x)] in the [MATH: x]-axis.

First, notice that the point [MATH: P(2, -1)] lies [MATH: 1] unit below the [MATH: x]-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected [MATH: 1] unit above the [MATH: x]-axis.

[IMG: /graphics/c4105ff195b571150972216deab7d412]

We conclude that the point [MATH: (2,1)] must lie on the graph of [MATH: y=-f(x).]
